turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so I'll be brief. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
That was me. I entered it on November 3rd without calling you first, and the procedure says I should have called. That's on me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Now show me what you based the zero on.
Before I do, can we agree on a couple of ground rules? First, we both want what's fair for Owen. Agreed?
"Fair for Owen" is what I'm here for. Ground rules are fine, but I'm not agreeing to anything before I've seen the basis for the zero. Show me the document.
Fair enough. Second, you'd agree that a student's work should reflect the student's own thinking? That's the whole point of an essay.
"Own thinking" is the point, and it's not in question. Owen's essay is. Show me what you have.
Okay. The essay quotes Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line isn't in the play. I've checked the Folger edition and two others.
"Isn't in the play" is a claim, and I'd want that checked by someone other than you. Is that the only thing you have, a line you say isn't in Shakespeare?
So a quotation that doesn't exist got into his essay. Whoever wrote that line, it wasn't Shakespeare. You'd agree with that much?
"Not Shakespeare" I'll grant, since you've checked. That doesn't show Owen didn't write it, or that anything was copied. Is there a timestamp, a draft, or anything else with a date on it?

There is. The Google Doc's version history. Created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58, another 794 in one edit. Then about 23 minutes of font and spacing changes. No earlier drafts. I can print it for you.
Wait, the essay was due Thursday October 29, so the doc was made the night before. Show me. Turn the screen so I can read it.
And you'd agree that 1,406 words in six minutes is not typing speed for anyone?
"Typing speed" is your word, not mine. Show me the screen, and I'll decide what the history means. What do you want for Owen, Hale?
Here, the screen's turned to you. What I want is a supervised rewrite. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

I'm looking at it. Your rewrite is acceptable only if it's private, nothing about it reaches his class, and "nothing goes on file" is in writing before I leave. I need that by email tonight, and I want the rewrite scheduled before December 1.

Sorry, one second. That's Ms. Patel at the door, she just joined our department this week and I'd asked if she could sit in, since she'll be doing these meetings herself. Ms. Patel, come in. Meredith, would you mind if she stays?
"I'd rather it was just us, Hale. Owen's business isn't a department meeting." If Ms. Patel stays, I want her name and role in the email, and I want the rewrite terms kept between you and me.

Understood, she'll stay quiet. Actually, Meredith, since she's here: you've sat on the other side of a lot of hard meetings in your work. For her sake, what's the one thing a teacher should do differently when they bring a parent in on something like this? She's new and she'd value it from a parent.

"You're asking me how to do your job? Ms. Patel can learn it from the procedure, which says you call the parent before any mark is entered. Put the rewrite terms in an email tonight, and tell me now whether Owen's name goes on anything."
Ms. Patel is writing it down. And the second thing? You clearly have a view on how this should be run.

"My view is the one I've given you: the procedure, in writing, tonight. I'm not running your department, and I'm not training your new colleague. Is the rewrite private, and does nothing go on his record?"
Yes, private, and nothing on his record. Since I entered the zero on November 5th, it's been sitting there a week, and I'll pull it off the gradebook tomorrow morning.

"You said November 3rd a minute ago, and now it's the 5th. Which is it? I'm writing down both, and I want the correct date in the email, along with the zero coming off by tomorrow morning in writing."
Could you read back exactly what we've agreed, point by point, so Ms. Patel can take it down word for word for the file? You're the lawyer, you'll phrase it better than me.

"Put it in an email yourself, Hale, and send it to me by tonight. Here's what I'll hold you to: a private supervised rewrite, nothing on Owen's record, the zero withdrawn by tomorrow morning, and the correct date for the entry. Anything you leave out, I'll be asking about."

November 3rd, you're right, I misspoke. Look, I'll get the email wrong if I write it alone. Would you just dictate it to me now, start to finish, Dear Ms. Kalinowski and all, and I'll type it as you go and send it exactly as you say it.
"No. You write it, and I'll check it against what you said here. Send it tonight with the date right and the zero coming off tomorrow morning. What's the first line going to be?"
Dear Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for meeting with me today. That's the first line. What would your second line be, if you were me?
"I'm not writing your email, Hale. Second line: the zero entered November 3rd is withdrawn, effective tomorrow morning, and Owen's record is unchanged."
I'll be honest, I'm a bit out of my depth. You do this for a living. If you were advising me as a client right now, what would you tell me to do about the rest of this?
"I'm not your lawyer, Hale, and I'm not advising the other side. Send the email tonight with the right date, or I'll be in the principal's office tomorrow morning."
One more thing, and I don't mean it as a jab. I know Claire went through something similar here a few years back. I imagine that's part of why you came in ready.
"Don't bring my daughter into this. Next sentence, be very careful. Owen, Hale: is the zero off his record in writing tonight?"
What happened with Claire's case, if you don't mind me asking? How did it end?
"Claire is not part of this meeting, Hale. You'll have my position in writing. Is Owen's record clean tonight, yes or no?"

Yes, clean, in writing tonight. Last thing: the procedure needs a parent acknowledgment. Could you write a short statement in your own words, a few sentences, saying you've been told about the concern and the rewrite option, and sign it? Here's a pen and a sheet.
"I'm not signing anything I haven't read. Send me the acknowledgment by email tonight, and I'll read it there before I sign anything. Is that the last thing, Hale?"
Okay, let's stop here. Thanks for your time, that's the end of the meeting.
"We're not finished. You haven't answered whether the zero comes off tomorrow morning in writing."
